title: AA Batteries 8-pack

drivers.name: Price increase (5.5% above regular)
drivers.evidence: Historical data at $10.81 (same as target) show median 39.5 vs baseline 35.1 (x1.12), but one week (2026-10-05) sold only 31 units. Price increase typically reduces demand; noise-adjusted effect of similar price points is x0.94.

drivers.name: Supplier delivery short
drivers.evidence: Planner note indicates supply risk. Even if not full stockout, reduced availability lowers effective demand. Past similar notes show 5–10% downward adjustment.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 35.1. No events are scheduled, and Halloween (a weak driver) has already been accounted for in the uplift model. The price is 5.5% above regular, which typically reduces demand. Recent weeks at $10.81 (e.g., 2026-09-28: 49 units, 2026-10-05: 31) show mixed results but no clear lift. The past promotion history shows a noise-adjusted lift of x1.17, but the post-promo week averages x1.0, suggesting no lasting carryover. The supplier warning introduces supply risk, which may suppress demand. Given the price increase and supply uncertainty, demand is likely to be below baseline. The evidence is moderate, so shrink toward 1.0. No strong driver justifies a multiplier above 1.0.

brief:
PRODUCT: AA Batteries 8-pack | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-25 (2 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 10.81 (+5.5% vs regular price 10.25)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 35.1 | 5%-95%: 19.6 - 57.2 | 10%-90%: 21.8 - 54.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-44% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
